note: npm audit --json, run from the repo root (one npm-workspaces tree spanning backend and frontend): ZERO vulnerable package names, and this baseline is therefore EMPTY. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-18 on the NestJS 12 upgrade branch. All six entries this file carried on 2026-09-15 (multer plus the five @nestjs/* names downstream of it) were deleted by this ratchet's own stale-entry rule, and UNLIKE the two deletions recorded before them, this one WAS earned by a change in this repository: the single root cause is gone at the source. Every one of the six traced to multer@2.2.0's four advisories (GHSA-wc9g-mqfw-jrwm, GHSA-qfvm-cv95-jqjf, GHSA-535w-7cp7-47q4, GHSA-qvfw-j98x-7q72), all four fixed together in multer 2.3.0, which the previous note recorded as unreachable because @nestjs/platform-express@11.2.3 pinned multer to the EXACT string "2.2.0" and a simple root override could not out-rank it. That note named three ways out and called the choice a repository-owner decision rather than a verification task's: a nested per-parent override, A NESTJS V12 UPGRADE, or a formally accepted risk. The second was taken. @nestjs/platform-express@12.0.3 pins multer 2.4.0 (confirmed: `npm view @nestjs/platform-express@12.0.3 dependencies.multer` prints "2.4.0"), which is past 2.3.0, so the vulnerable code is no longer in the tree at all — the image upload path through FileInterceptor (backend/src/media, 10 MB cap) now runs on a fixed multer rather than a recorded-but-unfixed one. This is a smaller RISK, not merely a narrower report, which is the distinction the 2026-09-15 note drew for the opposite case and the reason it is drawn again here. The ratchet's two directions are unchanged: a new advisory not listed here fails scripts/verify/checks/audit.mjs, and a listed entry npm audit no longer reports fails it too — which is precisely what emptied this file rather than leaving six forgivenesses standing.
